color.$description: Primitive color ramps. Mode-agnostic. Engineers and LLMs do NOT consume these directly — use semantic aliases (color.surface.*, color.text.*, etc.) instead. Lumen v0.4 retunes brand to obsidian (warm near-black, never navy) and warm to cream (warm paper). Accent unchanged: #4ade80 stays the brand value.

brand.$description: Obsidian — the dark canvas ramp for v0.4. Slightly warm-leaning near-black; replaces the v0.1–v0.3 Warp navy ladder. The dark-mode silhouette and the deep-ink moments in light mode.

accent.$description: Warp lime green. The only loud color in the system. Reads as 'laser' against obsidian without leaving the brand. Reserved for action / live / success. Never used decoratively.

300.$description: Laser highlight — used on dark for emphasis

400.$description: Warp --warp-accent (canonical brand accent, used 788x in Warp CSS)

500.$description: Same as 400 — convention to keep the brand value at the 500 step

600.$description: Hover state observed in Warp CSS

800.$description: Accent text on light surfaces (passes 4.7:1 on white)

warm.$description: Cream — paper-warm neutrals. Light-mode canvas + warm-tinted accents on dark. Replaces the v0.3 'gray' family.

status.$description: Status palette. Always paired with a label or shape — never used as the sole signal. v0.4 drops the sky-blue info hue; info now rides the cream/lime warm-neutral spectrum.

info.$description: Info hue — warm cream. v0.4 dropped sky-blue (no second loud color, no navy partnership).

alpha.$description: Translucent overlays. Used for scrims, blurred chrome, ticker fades, and the lime ambient glow.

12.$description: Subtle accent tint (card hover, table row tint)

24.$description: The signature green-glow opacity used by Warp under primary CTAs

danger.$description: v0.6 — translucent error halos. Used by input error rings + danger overlays.
